storyboard.claim: Believing unemployment will last a long time leads both Nora and Kevin into genuine depression.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock representing an agonizingly long, permanent time horizon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from the downsizing and high permanence scores of both accountants.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock marks the perception of permanence: time stretching out indefinitely without work.

storyboard.claim: Kevin had a drastically different pervasiveness score than Nora.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum diagram showing Nora low on pervasiveness (specific) and Kevin high (universal).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Kevin's explanatory style with Nora's on the pervasiveness axis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visually plots the two accountants on opposite ends of the pervasiveness spectrum.

storyboard.claim: Despite depression over permanent job loss, Nora maintained her spatial boundaries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield representing protective boundaries containing the failure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Nora's specific containment strategy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield clarifies that spatial boundaries act as an active defense preventing contagion.

storyboard.claim: She acknowledged being an unemployed accountant without letting it redefine her entire existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Nora calmly acknowledges her job status without despair.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details how Nora cognitively isolates her career loss from her self-worth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows her composed demeanor refusing to let a professional role consume her identity.

storyboard.claim: Nora kept up her workout routine and remained an engaged, loving spouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heart icon representing ongoing warmth and active devotion in her marriage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Provides concrete proof of the unaffected domains in Nora's daily life.
storyboard.addedInformation: The heart highlights that her domestic relationship remained completely intact and vibrant.

storyboard.claim: Nora contained the failure to professional life, while Kevin let it become a universal indictment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Nora indicates the boundary of work while Kevin slumps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Nora's containment with Kevin's total collapse.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual contrast of Nora standing firm versus Kevin succumbing to global failure.

storyboard.claim: Kevin stopped exercising, ignored his family, and withdrew from all social circles.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kevin isolated in a dark bedroom slumping in complete withdrawal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Traces the devastating consequences of Kevin's high pervasiveness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the domestic collapse resulting from failing to maintain cognitive boundaries.

storyboard.claim: One specific professional setback incinerated his universal world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A roaring fire icon representing total destruction across all life areas.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes Kevin's universalization as a fire consuming his life.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire makes the total devastation across Kevin's non-work domains tangible.

storyboard.claim: He catastrophized, raising the question of whether hyper-compartmentalizing carries risk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — everyday professional considering the dilemma of compartmentalization.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from Kevin's story to the listener's skeptical inquiry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the transition from clinical case to practical skepticism.

storyboard.claim: Am I compartmentalizing a real personal flaw by calling it specific?
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — everyman nervously questioning his own recurring workplace difficulties.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the counter-argument that repeated failures might point to systemic flaws.
storyboard.addedInformation: Presents the genuine fear that specificity might merely be rationalization.

storyboard.claim: Questioning whether this is a recurring personal pattern rather than bad luck.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stern boss pointing accusingly at the employee in an office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the objection about evading self-correction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual confrontation emphasizing the risk of dismissing genuine constructive criticism.

storyboard.claim: Pervasiveness is not ignoring patterns; it is preventing immediate systemic shutdown, like medical triage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Medical cross icon in a hospital clinic setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Seligman reframes spatial containment through a clinical emergency metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The medical cross reinforces the triage concept: treat the wound before the whole body shuts down.

storyboard.claim: Allowing a work flaw to convince you that you are a terrible father and unlovable spouse is high pervasiveness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — everyman slumping under the weight of runaway negative self-attributions.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Illustrates the toxic leap from professional flaw to personal worthlessness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the emotional slump of letting one localized failure contaminate unrelated roles.

storyboard.claim: High pervasiveness takes a localized infection and allows it to escalate into systemic sepsis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram mapping local infection progressing to systemic sepsis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the biological analogy of psychological pervasiveness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clarifies the dangerous escalation mechanism through cause-and-effect flow.

storyboard.claim: Spatial containment, keeping the failure specific, is the second half of cognitive hygiene.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A protective shield guarding against psychological spillover.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Formalizes spatial containment as an essential psychological tool.
storyboard.addedInformation: The held shield demonstrates active containment shielding life domains.

storyboard.claim: Containment preserves emotional energy and stability to fix workplace flaws because marriage and health remain intact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon showing clear focus on constructive behavioral goals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the listener's objection by showing containment enables real self-correction.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target icon visualizes directing energy toward deliberate self-improvement.

storyboard.claim: The third and final pillar of the internal grammar is personalization.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter diagram displaying the three pillars: Permanence, Pervasiveness, Personalization.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from the second pillar to introducing personalization.
storyboard.addedInformation: Groups the three pillars together to clarify their architectural relationship.

storyboard.claim: A scene: out to dinner with your partner who is unusually quiet, pushing food around.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A food plate with utensils representing a quiet dinner setting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the scene for testing internal versus external blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The food icon establishes the mundane domestic dinner scenario.

storyboard.claim: Internal dialogue takes over: 'I'm so boring, I never know what to talk about.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — everyman looking downward in anxious self-critical thought.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates the automatic internal blaming response.
storyboard.addedInformation: Portrays internal monologue spiraling into self-reproach.

storyboard.claim: This is internal blame versus external attribution, the axis that regulates self-esteem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance scale weighing internal fault against external circumstances.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Frames the dinner monologue as a prime example of personalization.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance scale visually weights self-blame against outside causes.

storyboard.claim: When negative events are interpreted as reflections of personal inadequacy, self-esteem collapses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — everyman engaged in painful, self-critical contemplation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how an internalizing explanatory style harms self-worth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the subjective experience of inadequacy eroding confidence.

storyboard.claim: Internalizing leads straight to destructive self-loathing, making you the villain in every story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mirror reflecting harsh, critical self-scrutiny.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Identifies the psychological endpoint of unchecked internal blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror signifies self-image distorted by relentless self-accusation.

storyboard.claim: Seligman details the gut-wrenching story of Elizabeth, a brilliant college student.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An academic book representing Elizabeth's scholarly promise.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Elizabeth as the focal case study for personalization.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book and academic setting establish her intellectual potential.

storyboard.claim: She had a casual exploratory conversation about Jane Austen with her academic adviser.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Elizabeth engaged in an animated, cheerful discussion with her professor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the innocent starting point of Elizabeth's academic tragedy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the friendly academic environment that misled Elizabeth.

callout.text: THE PROFESSOR SHARES HIS OWN ARTICLE

storyboard.claim: The professor brings in his own published manuscript for the student to read.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Research notes and papers held by the professor.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE PROFESSOR SHARES HIS OWN ARTICLE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the professor's critical omission during the discussion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The notes represent the unpublished academic work withheld from Elizabeth.

storyboard.claim: Believing it was an organic brainstorming session, Elizabeth used those ideas in her thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A thesis book representing her written academic submission.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Traces how the shared ideas ended up inside her dissertation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Elizabeth proudly holding her completed thesis volume.

storyboard.claim: Three days before graduation, the professor reported her to the committee for plagiarism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A law gavel icon representing formal disciplinary action.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sudden accusation crashing down on Elizabeth.
storyboard.addedInformation: The law icon highlights formal institutional prosecution.

storyboard.claim: He sandbags her, setting up a test of how different explanatory styles process trauma.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Elizabeth stunned and reeling from the unexpected betrayal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Captures the shock of the ambush before analyzing cognitive reactions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Elizabeth reeling from the betrayal of academic trust.

storyboard.claim: An optimistic externalizer would be rightfully furious, recognizing they were set up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — an indignant student pointing out the blatant injustice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Elizabeth's reaction with how a healthy externalizer would respond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Depicts active anger and recognition of external fault.

storyboard.claim: The professor was unprofessional and acted out of ego and malice to sabotage her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A false mask revealing the professor's hidden malice behind academic authority.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Exposes the true motive behind the plagiarism charge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask identifies bad faith disguised as institutional integrity.

storyboard.claim: They would fight back, hire a lawyer, and externalize blame where it rightfully belonged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield representing active legal and cognitive defense against unjust attack.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Demonstrates the self-protective actions generated by an externalizing style.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield demonstrates standing up to protect one's rights and reputation.

storyboard.claim: Elizabeth possessed a severe internalizing style, absorbing guilt and dredging up seventh-grade memories.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Elizabeth isolated in her bedroom ruminating on past missteps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the hypothetical fighter with Elizabeth's devastating internal collapse.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the psychological spiral of hunting for historical proof of inadequacy.

callout.text: I HAVE ALWAYS BEEN A FRAUD

storyboard.claim: She told herself: 'I'm a cheat. I've always been a fraud. I deserve this.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Elizabeth slumping in total self-condemnation.
storyboard.onScreenText: I HAVE ALWAYS BEEN A FRAUD
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quotes Elizabeth's catastrophic automatic thoughts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Portrays internal self-condemnation reaching catastrophic conclusions.

storyboard.claim: She stayed silent, lost her degree, and worked retail, abandoning her academic dreams.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Elizabeth sitting blank and defeated after giving up her aspirations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tragic life outcome produced by unchecked internalization.
storyboard.addedInformation: A blank, numb expression shows the total surrender caused by learned helplessness.

storyboard.claim: If we train people to externalize everything, don't we create a cultural blind spot?
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — conversational question on the danger of universal external blame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises a counter-objection to externalizing blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Raises the risk of creating entitled individuals who evade responsibility.

storyboard.claim: Are we engineering a society of raging narcissists who refuse accountability?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A narcissistic mask being challenged and rejected.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the objection about unchecked blame-shifting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The struck callout and mask challenge the caricature of irresponsible optimism.

storyboard.claim: There is a nuanced line between genuine productive responsibility and reflexively assuming total blame.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance scale weighing appropriate accountability against self-blame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Seligman draws the essential distinction between responsibility and self-blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance scale represents proportional, realistic attribution.

storyboard.claim: Personalization is the trickiest pillar because it is the easiest to fake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — Seligman explaining the subtlety of the personalization axis to the host.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Notes the superficial nature of outward blame deflection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the difference between verbal bravado and genuine explanatory habit.

storyboard.claim: You can superficially deflect blame out loud to protect ego while privately collapsing inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None — an executive smirking outwardly while hiding defensive insecurity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how fake externalizing masks deeper cognitive vulnerability.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirking posture captures superficial ego defense.

storyboard.claim: Combining internal personalization with permanence and pervasiveness creates the blueprint for clinical depression.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains representing the psychological trap of all three pessimistic dimensions combined.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Unifies the three pillars into the full cognitive architecture of depression.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains visually bind all three dimensions into severe depressive paralysis.
